problem_text:
A logistics manager must assemble a shipment of cargo containers to maximize total profit while adhering to a total freight weight limit.

The available containers are:
* Container A: weight 13kg, profit 271 units
* Container B: weight 42kg, profit 212 units
* Container C: weight 27kg, profit 171 units
* Container D: weight 7kg, profit 61 units
* Container E: weight 42kg, profit 133 units
* Container F: weight 21kg, profit 52 units
* Container G: weight 41kg, profit 101 units
* Container H: weight 12kg, profit 282 units
* Container I: weight 16kg, profit 258 units
* Container J: weight 34kg, profit 57 units
* Container K: weight 28kg, profit 299 units
* Container L: weight 33kg, profit 128 units
* Container M: weight 33kg, profit 181 units
* Container N: weight 18kg, profit 273 units
* Container O: weight 25kg, profit 237 units
* Container P: weight 7kg, profit 299 units
* Container Q: weight 1kg, profit 219 units
* Container R: weight 6kg, profit 186 units
* Container S: weight 19kg, profit 289 units
* Container T: weight 48kg, profit 39 units
* Container U: weight 4kg, profit 200 units
* Container V: weight 12kg, profit 60 units
* Container W: weight 16kg, profit 193 units
* Container X: weight 34kg, profit 27 units
* Container Y: weight 49kg, profit 179 units
* Container Z: weight 36kg, profit 130 units
* Container AA: weight 37kg, profit 124 units
* Container BB: weight 21kg, profit 55 units
* Container CC: weight 44kg, profit 51 units
* Container DD: weight 4kg, profit 60 units

Furthermore, due to a contractual exclusivity clause, exactly one of Container A and Container B must be included in the shipment.

If Container C is selected, the permitted total freight weight is effectively diminished by 10 kg.
The transport vehicle can handle a maximum of 510 kg. The manager must determine which containers to load.
